name: Thomas Sankara
role: Burkinabe army captain and revolutionary; president of Upper Volta/Burkina Faso (1983-1987)
summary: Marxist-influenced anti-imperialist and pan-Africanist who led a military-backed popular revolution in Burkina Faso. His programme combined self-reliance, rejection of foreign debt and aid, land nationalization, mass health and literacy campaigns, reforestation, women's emancipation and an austere style of rule, enforced through CDRs and revolutionary tribunals that curtailed opposition, unions and chiefs.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Listed 'health for everyone' as an objective of the revolution, and his government built a clinic in every village and ran mass vaccination campaigns.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Called for an independent, self-sufficient and planned national economy and for popular control of production and distribution circuits, rejecting reliance on market allocation.

public-ownership.rationale: Programme called for progressively establishing popular control over production and distribution in the modern sector, and the state ran the rail-building and state supermarket projects; energy and utilities were not discussed by name.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: His government cut the pay of well-off civil servants (including his own) and obliged them to give a month's salary to public projects, and tribunals prosecuted tax evasion; no general tax-rate statement found.

unions-good.rationale: Said he counted on progressive unions but would block reactionary ones, and unions were later placed under CDR authority; the evidence points both ways.

property-fundamental.rationale: Nationalized all land in August 1984 and said private property in the old neocolonial order was a source of exploitation and speculation.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Described foreign private investment as draining wealth out of the country and called for effective popular control of production and distribution circuits.

strong-leader.rationale: Rejected the 'messianic vision' of one man changing the world and said he was no messiah, yet ruled by decree as a strong leader.

state-harmful.rationale: Said the building of a people's democratic state was the revolution's ultimate goal and relied on the state for health, education and planning.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: His government worked to eliminate prostitution, which he called a symbol of female slavery.

decide-locally.rationale: Programme promised decentralization and devolution of administrative power but kept democratic centralism with local autonomy within higher bodies' guidelines.

traditional-family.rationale: Described the patriarchal family as rooted in private property and women's oppression and said marriage is not indispensable.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Said women's inequality was produced by social organization, not physical difference, and that 'apparent physical weakness' results from imposed norms.

gradual-change.rationale: Said the revolution must be a total upheaval sparing no area of economic, social or cultural life.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Told the UN it must be strengthened and given the means to act, while also seeking to abolish the veto.

free-trade.rationale: Rejected unfair competition from imports and urged consumption of local products over imports.

nation-first.rationale: Said 'Burkina Faso for the Burkinabe' and 'Africa for Africans' but also stressed internationalism and solidarity.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Lamented that international brigades no longer defend attacked nations and wished African troops had backed Angola, yet condemned interventions in Afghanistan and Grenada.

revolution-justified.rationale: Led the August 1983 insurrection and called revolution the way to end neocolonial domination.

experts-over-public.rationale: Said forestry engineers and experts working alone achieve nothing and the struggle must be democratic and popular.

central-planning.rationale: Named a planned national economy as the aim and launched a Five-Year Popular Development Plan, while also promising remunerative prices to farmers.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Programme promised protection of local production from unfair competition by imports; his government banned some imports and promoted Burkinabe cotton cloth and food.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The Five-Year Plan directed about 71 percent of productive investment to agriculture, livestock and forestry; directed investment into strategic industries was not his stated formula.

one-party-rule.rationale: Dissolved the old regime's parties and spoke of building a revolutionary organization citing Lenin, but in 1985 doubted a party would stay combative and never made a single party the state.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Called traditional feudal chiefs a reactionary force and stripped the Mossi king and chiefs of executive and judicial powers.

democracy-best.rationale: Said his revolution was democratic and popular and rooted power in CDRs, but held no elections and dissolved old parties.

workers-councils.rationale: Inferred: he made the CDRs, organized in workplaces, villages and neighbourhoods, the organs of popular power replacing the old state machine; they were not workers' councils proper.

right-to-secede.rationale: Told the UN that Burkina Faso 'shall never accept any splitting up of our country'.

political-violence-never.rationale: Said the people would impose its will by force of arms if necessary and carried a pistol to a Harlem rally against imperialism.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Described the nation as many ethnic groups living in equality and vowed to fight ethnic prejudice and those who sow division.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Credited dialectical materialism and Engels for showing exploitation and women's status as products of class society and said society moves through class struggle.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Said Africa is owed a 'blood debt' that no wealth could repay, and told the UN that Africa and the Black world paid the cost of capitalism's rise.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Told revolutionaries to put the masses' interest before self-interest and counted individualism among evils to fight.

limit-population.rationale: Rejected Malthusian arguments but promoted family planning and lifted contraception restrictions.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Said 'we are not against progress' while opposing anarchic, rights-ignoring progress.

restore-past-order.rationale: Called for 'total upheaval' of society and attacked traditional feudal structures.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Insisted that the ideological basis of the struggle be clearly set out or work becomes empty talk.

direct-action.rationale: Took power by insurrection and spoke critically of CNR parliamentarism, though he built mass organizations and a state.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Described the state and commercial bourgeoisie as enriching themselves by exploiting labour, and foreign investment as extracting wealth from workers and peasants.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Said the revolution would impose the people's will by force of arms if needed on the exploiting classes, but framed the ruling power as an alliance of classes (the people), not the working class alone.

collective-farming.rationale: Government bought tractors for large cooperative projects and ran collective village labour, but the land reform kept peasants farming plots individually and he called for many small farms.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Said arguments from skin colour were invented as a supposedly scientific justification for domination.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Said 'there is no innocent writing' and 'there is no neutral information, no neutral cinema'.

universal-morality.rationale: Told the OAU 'the rich and the poor do not have the same morality'.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Called Zionism a form of racism, demanded Israel's suspension from the UN and backed the PLO, while saying he loved Israel's people.

rule-by-example.rationale: Stressed the moral example of revolutionaries and lived austerely himself, but also relied on tribunals and discipline.

national-self-determination.rationale: Backed every people's right to independence and to choose its government, naming the Sahrawi, Palestinians, Namibians and Comorians.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Said culture should draw on what is good in the past and tradition, while rejecting what is anti-national or anti-popular.

dominated-front.rationale: Urged a united African front against debt and spoke of a special solidarity uniting Asia, Latin America and Africa in one battle.

workers-nation.rationale: Practised and urged proletarian internationalism and said Europe's and Africa's masses share a common enemy.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Said men and women must share all household tasks and that equal pay and legal equality should be real.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Called apartheid a cancer to be exterminated and a form of modern Nazism.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Said the inherited state, army, courts and administration had been shaped to serve the reactionary classes and imperialism.

national-mission.rationale: Said the revolution was not imported or exported but later called for revolution in neighbouring Mali.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Described a system of exploitation imposed on women by men and said male power rests on economic and political organization.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Described the neocolonial ruling elite as a parasitic bourgeoisie practising corruption, nepotism and embezzlement.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Said 'nothing that is human is alien to me', called women fully equal to men and condemned racism.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Said the Palestinians were replaced by another people and endorsed describing Israel and South Africa as examples of anachronistic colonialism.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Spoke of popular sovereignty but took power by a military insurrection and held no elections.

trade-surplus.rationale: Treated a persistent trade deficit as ruinous ('we buy more abroad than we sell') and urged producing and consuming domestically.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Held that force of arms may be used against enemies of the revolution and nationalized land by decree.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Dissolved parties associated with the neocolonial regime on taking power; they were not defined as seeking to abolish the constitutional order.

vanguard-party.rationale: Cited Lenin that revolution needs revolutionary organization and ideology, yet in 1985 doubted a party would stay combative.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Centred his programme on peasants and the poorest and said he spoke for the disinherited of the world.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Called Malthusian arguments fallacious, said Africa is underpopulated and blamed an unjust social organization for poverty.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Blamed imperialist divide and rule, not diversity itself, for ethnic conflict and promoted union of different nationalities.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Revolutionary tribunals tried regime opponents with reduced protections and he defended them against French critics; he said the revolution would be authoritarian toward its enemies.

party-controls-media.rationale: Backed a 'responsible, militant press' and said there is no neutral information, but also said he did not want journalists to be sycophants.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Programme made democratic centralism, with lower bodies bound to higher ones, the guiding principle of the CDRs.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Urged African unity and an OAU front on debt, and began a process of merger with Ghana.

recall-officials.rationale: Inferred: told L'Humanité that CDRs deposed old authorities on proof of abuses and re-elected delegates.

people-in-arms.rationale: Said the people take on defence themselves, with the army only more specialized and all citizens trained militarily.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Described the African intellectual elite with foreign diplomas as unwilling to give up privileges and said a degree is no pass to emancipation.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Said cultures can complement each other harmoniously but historically unequal relations favoured the colonizer's.

death-penalty.rationale: In 1984 seven people tied to the former regime were executed for treason after a summary tribunal trial under his government.

minority-language-support.rationale: Wanted radio broadcast in the languages Burkinabe understand and the equal development of every region and nationality.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Told the OAU that the debt cannot and should not be repaid and urged a united front for outright cancellation.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Condemned aid with humiliating conditions and a beggar mentality but also demanded rich-country money for trees and development and said Africa is owed.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Treated wealth as legitimate only when serving the people: attacked rent-seeking, speculation and enrichment through the state, and said all wealth should be managed by the people.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Treated the USSR as an ally on the side of peace and workers' revolution, though he mentioned 'sad infringements of human rights' by some revolutions.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Condemned Morocco's treatment of Western Sahara, South Africa's occupation of Namibia and French hold on Mayotte, saying Mayotte belongs to the Comoros.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Opposed feudal claims of superiority by birth or divine right and the praise of leaders.

character-from-environment.rationale: Described how boys and girls are shaped by upbringing and social norms and that women's consciousness reflects economic structure.

space-expansion.rationale: Urged cutting space-research budgets and diverting 1 percent of them to saving trees and lives.

leader-cult.rationale: Told his own supporters to stop songs hoping he would be president forever, calling such praise feudal reflexes.

land-redistribution.rationale: Land reform aimed to abolish the traditional structures that oppress peasants and nationalized the land; no large estates were handed over as such.

moral-incentives.rationale: Said revolutionaries should expect no reward and put the masses before self-interest, and mobilized volunteer labour for dams and railways.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Took power with about 250 commandos but insisted it was a prepared popular insurrection, not a coup.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Attacked feudal hereditary structures and demoted the Mossi elite, though titles themselves were not abolished.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Wanted education to produce a Voltaic personality rid of mimicry and promoted Black peoples taking responsibility for their own history.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Attacked technical assistants as 'technical assassins' and colonial rule as plunder.

patriotic-education.rationale: Called for 'patriotic training' and national culture in schools and wrote a new anthem and flag for the country.

delink-world-market.rationale: Pursued self-sufficiency and import substitution but also called for trade with all countries on an equal footing.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Told the OAU that the popular masses of Europe are not opposed to Africa's masses and that those who exploit Africa exploit Europe too.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Said wealthy and educated women should place wealth and knowledge at the service of the people.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Demanded every citizen engage in revolutionizing their sphere and urged study and militancy.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Said Western films and media condition the people and that art is prostituted by show business.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Said the colonial school and media reproduced a society serving imperialism and that western opinion makers are kept on a leash by financiers.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Argued that aid, debt and foreign investment drain wealth from poor countries and that debt is a 'skillfully managed reconquest of Africa'.

party-own-road.rationale: Said every revolution has its own originality, that his was not imported, and that the country would keep from others' revolutions only their essence.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Said aid should help end the need for aid, refused to declare a disaster to receive relief, and called for relying on own resources.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Said he fought the idea that anything from the Soviet Union means totalitarianism, while calling South African and Israeli methods fascist.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Said Burkina Faso chose forms of organization better adapted to its civilization, rejecting outside diktats, and defended its tribunals against Western critics.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Gave the army an internal task of maintaining revolutionary order and safeguarding popular power and rejected an apolitical army.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Inferred: his programme said the elective principle applies at every level of CDRs, and delegates were re-elected when discredited.

land-use-tenure.rationale: His government nationalized all land in August 1984, ending chiefs' control over who may farm.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Criticised the capitalist consumer society, urged austerity and simple living, and called women's crass materialism a danger to the revolution.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Condemned all foreign intervention, naming the invasion of Afghanistan and the aggression against Grenada.

non-intervention.rationale: His programme listed non-intervention in internal affairs as a principle, though he urged African forces to help Angola and condemned the Afghan invasion.

local-production.rationale: Urged 'produce in Africa, transform in Africa, consume in Africa' and wore locally woven cloth to the OAU summit.

informal-organisation.rationale: Said revolution differs from anarchy and requires discipline, organization and committees with action plans.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Rejected deference to powers, demanding dignity and sovereignty in relations with France and others.

defeat-communism.rationale: Praised the Soviet Union, visited Moscow and rejected the claim that Soviet life means totalitarianism and misery.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Said women's liberation requires abolishing the system that exploits them and ties it to class exploitation.

socialized-care.rationale: Called for a large network of nurseries, day-care centres and cafeterias so housework does not trap women, and for men to share housework.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Described himself as armed with the ideology of the great educators of the proletariat and praised Cuba and the USSR, while insisting on an original path.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Told the UN that Jews were 'consigned to the horrors of the crematorium', accepting the Holocaust as fact.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Said reactionaries must be blocked whatever organization they hide in, including unions or underground parties; the government dissolved old parties and harassed unions.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Condemned colonialism as plunder of Africa and neocolonial rule as continued exploitation.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Pledged that nothing would be done without the people's participation through the CDRs, but held no elections and the committees enforced the regime's line; mixed.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Said at the OAU 'I would want us to disarm' though he was a soldier who built a revolutionary army.

rich-first.rationale: Described the country as 'paradise for some and hell for others' and sought to end the privilege of a rich minority.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Described Burkina Faso as one of the non-aligned countries acting free of hindrance by any of the big powers.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Denounced one-sided contracts and draconian conditions imposed by banks and urged African states to refuse to repay and go to the World Bank only to pay if they disagreed.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Said opinion-makers and media are held on a leash by those with financing and that information must be freed.

racial-franchise.rationale: Condemned South Africa's apartheid laws that excluded the black majority from rights.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Said men and women must share all tasks at home and women must not live under a man's 'colonial protectorate'.

rent-control.rationale: Programme called for halting exploitation through excessive rents and establishing reasonable rents.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Said imperialist listening centres and occupied ports on African soil must be driven out of Africa.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Condemned the bourgeoisie living on rents, speculation and embezzlement while workers' wages were consumed, and said productive work emancipates women.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Brandished a pistol in Harlem, saying its bullets would be fired against imperialism, and led an armed revolutionary army.

independent-unions.rationale: His government placed unions and NGOs under the authority of the CDRs and arrested union leaders; he said unions must not rival the CDRs.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Urged Black unity but said he fought apartheid not because he was Black but as a human taking the working class side.

racial-pride.rationale: Told a Harlem audience 'we must be proud to be black'.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Gave the army the external task of defending territorial integrity and called the 1974 Mali war unjust.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Described one Voltaic nation made of many ethnic groups with different languages and customs.

future-generations.rationale: Denounced colonial plunder of forests 'without the slightest thought of replenishing them for tomorrow' and organized mass tree planting.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Praised women's qualities and complementarity but said women have the same mix of qualities and weaknesses as men.

arms-reduction.rationale: Urged disarmament and limiting armaments among weak and poor countries and said military spending wastes resources.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Programme spoke of 'the weapons of the people' managed by the CDRs, which were organized as armed mass bodies.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Called at the UN for a new international economic order and a decision-making role for poor countries in trade, economic and monetary machinery.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Programme said the neocolonial state machine must be destroyed and a new one built to guarantee popular sovereignty.

farm-price-support.rationale: Promised remunerative prices and markets for farmers' produce in all seasons and had hundreds of village cereal banks built.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Removed chiefs' executive powers and called them forces of feudal reaction opposed to peasant emancipation.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: His government made arson of forests a crime, required tree planting, and regulated firewood cutting and livestock roaming.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Defined democracy as popular power exercised through CDRs rather than through competitive elections.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred: he said young unmarried mothers are unfairly blamed and single women should not be ostracized.

women-suffrage.rationale: Said women must take part at every level of decision-making and appointed women to government.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Listed entrenched religions among the institutions that wrote women out of history and excluded them, alongside property and capitalism.

race-social-construct.rationale: Said race-based arguments were a pretext for domination and apartheid, without addressing racial categories directly.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Created a family-development ministry and the Women's Union of Burkina but mocked an earlier women's ministry as a pseudo-ministry and wanted every ministry judged on women's equality.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred: his CDR structure had each level subordinate to the next up under democratic centralism with elected delegates.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Attacked corruption, nepotism and use of state power by the state bourgeoisie to benefit its own ventures.

national-resource-control.rationale: Said the people would be sole master of the nation's wealth and nationalized land; criticised foreign investment drawing revenue abroad.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Spoke in Harlem and at the UN of Black ghettos and racism as ongoing obstacles.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Joined 'Homeland or death' patriotism with a programme for peasants and workers.

notes: Historical figure: only positions he stated or enacted are answered; items marked 'Inferred:' follow directly from stated views. Speech translations on thomassankara.net are partly machine-translated. Views on party organization and democracy shifted across 1983-1987 (the 1985 doubts about a party versus the 1986 call for revolutionary organization); the later statement is used where clear. The record of repression (tribunals, executions, teacher dismissals, union arrests) rests on the Wikipedia article summarising secondary scholarship.
